# Ethernet Frame Corruption Recovery: How NICs Detect and Handle Invalid Frames
## Overview
Ethernet frame corruption recovery relies on physical layer mechanisms rather than trusting the frame's own headers. When a device receives a corrupted frame, it cannot trust any field—including length/type indicators—making boundary detection critical.
## How Corrupted Frames Are Handled
When the NIC detects a frame with invalid FCS:

1. **Frame reception continues** until the physical layer returns to IDLE pattern (inter-packet gap)
2. The NIC **discards the entire frame**—it cannot trust any contents including length fields
3. The receive error counter increments
4. Higher-layer protocols (TCP) handle retransmission; UDP applications may lose data

**Toolbox Talk Training: Scaffold Safety – Scaffolds: Keeping It All Together**

A scaffold is held together by braces, pins, couplers, and ties. This talk summarizes OSHA requirements for scaffold connections and bracing, and how to report problems. Federal scaffold rules are in OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart L (1926.450-.454) for construction; general industry scaffold work is covered by 29 CFR 1910.27 and 1910.28. Follow the manufacturer's instructions and your employer's rules.

**Frame scaffolds**

- Frames and panels must be braced by cross, horizontal, or diagonal braces, or a combination, that secure the vertical members together laterally. - Couplers must be structural metal, such as drop-forged steel, malleable iron, or structural grade aluminum. Gray cast iron is prohibited (1926.452(b)(9)).

Syed Talal Wasim Affiliation:Texas A&M University University of Bonn Affiliation:Lamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Juergen Gall Affiliation:Texas A&M University University of Bonn Affiliation:Lamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Erchin Serpedin Hasan Kurban Affiliation:Hamad Bin Khalifa University

###### Abstract

Vision-language models pass text-based false-belief probes at near-human levels but drop by over twenty percentage points on abstract panels the moment the same problem is conveyed visually. The consensus diagnosis is conceptual, prescribing new belief-reasoning modules. We argue the dominant bottleneck is perceptual: not what the model cannot reason about, but what it cannot see. We propose a five-condition dissociation protocol that holds the reasoning task constant while varying perceptual fidelity from visual only to text only, and quantify the result with the Perceptual Contribution Ratio, the share of the visual-to-text gap a given fidelity closes. We test this on two kinds of scenes: abstract 2D panels in the Heider–Simmel tradition, and naturalistic 3D game scenes from MuMA-ToM and MindPower. The evaluation covers seven VLMs and roughly 159,000 API calls. Ground-truth scaffolds substantially close the gap in every setting, and on the abstract panels and MuMA-ToM they match or exceed the text-only reasoning. Whereas scaffolds built by automatic parsers, including frontier VLMs, fail. The most common error in the visual-only condition is _reality bias_, which accounts for 60% of false-belief failures. Models report where an object actually is, not where an absent agent believes it is. This points to a perceptual front-end that fails to track which agents were present at each moment. Under the evaluated protocol, structured visual scene-state extraction, rather than belief inference, is the dominant bottleneck for visual ToM. octen.title: Generalist Open-World Temporal Perception
octen.snippet:
Cross-modal binding assigns observations to sources and referents: which object produced a sound, which person uttered particular words, or which visual and tactile observations concern the same contact event. Existing methods address such associations in specific settings; the broader challenge is to resolve competing sources and ambiguous references when several entities interact, relevant sources are unobserved, or modalities provide conflicting evidence. This requires distinguishing signals that merely co-occur from those attributable to the same underlying source, while retaining uncertainty when the observations do not determine a unique assignment.
The temporal gap.
Much of visual foundation modeling remains image-centric or short-context. Yet the world is not a collection of independent images. It is a temporally evolving process in which entities persist, deform, disappear, reappear, collide, interact, and cause sensory consequences across modalities. Static recognition cannot determine identity through occlusion, distinguish a transient texture from an object, infer a gait cycle, separate an action from its preparation, or identify the moment when one event causes another.
Temporal perception requires maintaining state. The system must infer what remains true when it is not visible, what has changed, what has remained identical, what is ambiguous, and what is likely to happen next. This is particularly demanding for articulated bodies, animals, tools, deformable materials, social interactions, and physical contact, where the relevant structure unfolds over time and is only partially visible in any single frame. A model that understands an event only by captioning the clip has not necessarily represented the event’s geometry, dynamics, or causal organization.

###### Abstract

Vision-language models pass text-based false-belief probes at near-human levels but drop by over twenty percentage points on abstract panels the moment the same problem is conveyed visually. The consensus diagnosis is conceptual, prescribing new belief-reasoning modules. We argue the dominant bottleneck is perceptual: not what the model cannot reason about, but what it cannot see. Models report where an object actually is, not where an absent agent believes it is. This points to a perceptual front-end that fails to track which agents were present at each moment. **X-bracing**, also called **cross bracing**, is a pair of diagonal braces that cross each other in an X shape between two frames, posts or uprights. On scaffolds, cross braces tie the vertical members together, keep the structure square and plumb, and resist racking, swaying and collapse under load.

Cross braces look like simple parts, but they carry real structural loads. Missing, loose or improvised braces are a common finding during scaffold inspections, and OSHA's scaffold rules in 29 CFR Part 1926, Subpart L, address how braces must be installed, when they can stand in for a guardrail and why they must never be climbed.

## What Is X-Bracing (Cross Bracing)?

Cross bracing is a method of stiffening a structure by adding two diagonal members that form an X across a rectangular bay. When a sideways force pushes on the frame, one brace is put into tension and the other into compression, which stops the rectangle from deforming into a parallelogram. That deformation is called racking.

The term is used across construction and industry. Steel buildings, towers, storage racks and temporary structures all use cross bracing. In workplace safety, the term most often refers to scaffolds, especially fabricated frame scaffolds (also called tubular welded frame scaffolds), where manufactured cross braces pin onto studs on each end frame. Cross braces also appear on mobile scaffolds, pole scaffolds, tube and coupler scaffolds and tiered horse scaffolds.

## Why Cross Bracing Matters

A scaffold's strength depends on its components working together. Braces lock the frames into a single rigid unit. Without them, frames can lean, legs can buckle and the platform can shift or collapse.

## The Invariant Interval: Classifying Event Pairs and Reading Causal Structure

#### Events and their separations

An event is a point in spacetime: a place and a time, specified in some inertial frame by coordinates (t,x)(t, x). Two events have coordinate separations Δt\Delta t and Δx\Delta x, and both are generally frame-dependent: a different inertial frame may assign a different value to either separation or to both.

One combination of them, however, is the same for everyone.

#### The invariant interval

For two events separated along one spatial direction, define

 Δs2=c2Δt2−Δx2 \boxed{\ \Delta s^{2} = c^{2}\Delta t^{2} - \Delta x^{2}\ }

This quantity, the spacetime interval, takes the same value in every inertial frame. Two observers in relative motion generally obtain different coordinate separations, though an individual Δt\Delta t or Δx\Delta x can coincide for a particular event pair and boost.

They agree exactly about Δs2\Delta s^{2}. Its invariance is a consequence of the Lorentz transformations; that derivation belongs to the sibling concept, and what matters here is the use to which the invariant is put.

Two notational cautions. Some texts use the opposite sign convention, Δs2=Δx2−c2Δt2\Delta s^{2} = \Delta x^{2} - c^{2}\Delta t^{2}, which reverses the sign inequalities associated with timelike and spacelike separations; the physical labels remain unchanged, so always check which convention a source is using.

And Δs2\Delta s^{2} is a single symbol for a quantity that may be negative, it is not the square of a real number Δs\Delta s in every case, which is exactly why the three cases below are distinguished.

Keeping the units consistent matters in practice. Multiply times by cc so that c Δtc\,\Delta t is a length, and the interval is a difference of two squared lengths.

Double pole (independent pole) scaffold means a supported scaffold consisting of a platform(s) resting on cross beams (bearers) supported by ledgers and a double row of uprights independent of support (except ties, guys, braces) from any structure.
Brace means a rigid connection that holds one scaffold member in a fixed position with respect to another member, or to a building or structure. Bricklayers' square scaffold means a supported scaffold composed of framed squares which support a platform.
Interior hung scaffold means a suspension scaffold consisting of a platform suspended from the ceiling or roof structure by fixed length supports. Ladder jack scaffold means a supported scaffold consisting of a platform resting on brackets attached to ladders. Ladder stand means a mobile, fixed-size, self-supporting ladder consisting of a wide flat tread ladder in the form of stairs. Landing means a platform at the end of a flight of stairs. Large area scaffold means a pole scaffold, tube and coupler scaffold, systems scaffold, or fabricated frame scaffold erected over substantially the entire work area.

you.title: r/networking on Reddit: Ethernet frame corruption recovery
you.snippet:
Posted by u/Ill-Language2326 - 32 votes and 45 comments
How does a a device recover from a corrupted Ethernet frame? The header contains a 32 bit CRC. If the device computes it and it doesn't match the one in the frame, it means the frame is corrupted, and since it cannot know what field got corrupted, it cannot trust anything written in it.
And by the time your throwing many errors the whole channel is stuffed anyway. Yes multiple if a post and a pre are broken sequentially 2 frames could land in the frame buffer and it thinks its 1 frame and discards the lot. Eventually it gets greater than buffer and just discards it anyway until you get to next preample.
